title: Enterprise Ask Stitcher and First-pass Implementation Map
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summarize and normalize a batch of high-touch enterprise feature requests from Sales/CS into a small set of consolidated solution threads, produce a first-pass implementation map for each thread (estimate effort, infra impact, data residency/security considerations), and validate the consolidation with the originating AEs/CSMs. Goal: reduce duplicate scoping work, speed sales responses, and create repeatable artifacts for Dedicated/Private eligibility checks.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidation: 15 incoming enterprise asks (sample window) are grouped into <= 5 solution threads with documented rationale
Implementation map: For each thread, an implementation map exists covering API changes, runtime requirements, storage/retention implications, and a rough engineering T-shirt estimate (S/M/L/XL)
Risk flags: Identify any compliance/KMS/data residency/security blockers per thread and classify severity (none/low/medium/high)
Stakeholder validation: AE/CSM owners have signed off on the thread grouping and the priority order for a pilot
Pilot plan: A 6-week pilot plan and acceptance metrics (time-to-proposal, estimated infra delta, revenue capture signal) are documented and scheduled with Eng + Solutions
work_items: Collect last 90 days of enterprise feature asks from Sales Lanes and CSM intake form
Canonicalize request attributes (account size, SLA ask, data residency, model type, concurrency need)
Run clustering heuristic to surface similar asks; manually review clusters with 2 PMs
Draft implementation map template and populate for each solution thread
Host validation workshop with originating AEs/CSMs and Solutions Engineering
Publish consolidated intake artifact and pilot plan to Confluence and link to shared Drive
comments: 2025-11-03 - Ava Chen: Kicked off collection; pulled 42 raw tickets from Sales pipe and 18 CSM emails. Initial dedupe reduced to 27 unique asks. Created canonical CSV in Drive.

2025-11-05 - Liam Patel: Ran clustering run (TF-IDF + manual heuristics). Found 6 obvious clusters; 3 clusters are cross-account policy/permissions asks that likely map to RBAC/audit work rather than runtime.

2025-11-06 - Sophie Laurent: Security review note - several asks request cross-account data joins and external tool integrations; flagged for KMS and data residency checks. Marked two clusters as 'compliance-high'.

2025-11-07 - Dr. Omar Haddad: Solutions draft suggests two viable implementation paths for the 'model variants routing' thread: runtime fallback vs. API-level model aliasing + orchestration. Runtime fallback has lower product change but higher infra cost; API aliasing needs more product design.

2025-11-09 - Priya Nair (CSM): Confirmed that consolidating these four asks into one 'dedicated routing + access controls' thread is acceptable for EMEA accounts; they prefer rollout with a clear audit log path.

2025-11-10 - Liam Patel: Populated implementation map template for 5 threads. Estimated effort: two threads S, two M, one L. Noted ENG dependency ENG-4123 for auth scaffolding and ENG-4218 for KV cache sizing.
2025-11-11 - Elliot Rivera: Provided commercial context for two accounts that would pay for expedited delivery (approx. $75k ARR within first 12 months) — added to pilot priority.
2025-11-12 - Ava Chen: Scheduled cross-functional triage workshop 2025-11-14. Next actions: finalize pilot acceptance metrics and create a 1-pager to share with CRO and Solutions leadership.
next_steps: Run one-hour cross-functional workshop 2025-11-14 (agenda uploaded to Drive link)
Refine pilot acceptance metrics and finalize the 6-week pilot cohort (3 accounts) by 2025-11-18
Spin up scoped RFC in /docs/rfcs for the highest-priority thread and assign ENG owners
Create a templated intake form with required fields for future high-touch asks (link in Confluence)
Prepare a short executive summary for CRO + Head of Sales by 2025-11-20
